chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Gundar, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about kohl (eye makeup) for the fasting person. He said: There is no harm with it, for it is not food that is eaten.

key_terms.الْكُحْلِ: Kohl, a traditional eye cosmetic applied to the eyelids or under the eyes
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does applying kohl break the fast in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that applying kohl does not break the fast because it is not classified as 'food' (طعام) in the juristic sense, distinguishing between external application and internal consumption. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the specific mechanism of breaking the fast—namely, the ingestion of nourishment—rather than mere entry of substances into the body. It reflects the broader principle of *al-asl al-sihha* (presumption of validity) in fasting rituals, ensuring that minor cosmetic practices do not invalidate the spiritual act of worship.
